details:
This bug has been present for a while but I've been testing and gathering evidence.
When you have an avatar with toggle-able Parameters that are controlled by Integers and Booleans, and you walk through a teleporter within a world, in your own camera the Integer and Boolean value will cycle to 0 and False respectively for a split second before it resets to its proper value.
This means that if you have an avatar with toggle states for clothes, and you walk through a teleporter, your clothes will disappear for a split second before they reappear. If there is an animated transition, it will go through whatever animation you've set for when the Integer/Boolean goes to 0/False and then back to its proper value.
This only happens in your own camera when looking at yourself. Your first person view shows no bug, and other users do not see the bug in their 1st person view nor their cameras.
I've uploaded 2 recordings of this bug occurring. My avatars are set to play a transition animation when I toggle to and from Integers and Booleans 0 and False to other values and True respectively. The first link shows how it only happens in the camera view and not 1st person view, and the 2nd link shows it happening in a different world.
https://youtu.be/D5Wblgi4fMc
https://youtu.be/wWUi3MgY4CE
Not recorded is my testing with a friend to see if they see my toggles cycling, but they reported that they didn't see anything happen while my camera was still showing my animations playing.
Testing teleporters in older world that use older SDKs do not cause this bug. This bug is only replicate-able in worlds uploaded with newer World SDKs.
title: [BUG] Integer and Boolean values cycle to 0 and False in own camera's view when getting teleported in newer World SDKs
